series_items.subject: [RFC PATCH 1/1] mm/swap: allocate contiguous swap slots for a reclaim batch
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses the issue of scattered swap slot allocations, which can lead to inefficient write requests and increased latency in workloads that rewrite swapped out memory. To mitigate this, it introduces a new approach where contiguous swap slots are allocated for each reclaim batch, following the order-0 allocation strategy. The patch modifies various kernel modules, including mm/shmem.c, mm/swap.h, mm/swapfile.c, and mm/vmscan.c, to implement this new behavior. It also adds new functions to prepare and split swap allocations, as well as updates existing functions to work with the new approach.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch aims to reduce the number of I/O requests on a swap device by keeping reclaim batches contiguous. The current implementation of swap allocation and deallocation can lead to scattered writes, resulting in increased I/O requests. The patch modifies the allocator to allocate contiguous free slots for a reclaim batch, reducing the number of small requests and improving throughput. This is achieved by informing the allocator about the size of the batch and allowing it to allocate contiguous slots accordingly. The goal is to reduce the overhead of swap I/O operations and improve system performance.

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song suggested reverting commit 9a42aed48421, which prefers nonfull over free clusters for small order allocations, and instead always scanning full clusters to prioritize contiguity on large physical swap devices.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Alexandre,

That's a interesting problem. I think the real problem is with commit
9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters"), right?

It's more like a balance between fragmentation and contiguity of small
order allocation issue.

Perhaps we should instead always scan the full clusters and revert
that one commit? That commit was only following the idea of keeping
the allocation more compacted for that series, it looked good at that
time. Since fragmentation issues can be solved in other ways,
contiguity seems to matter more for large physical swap devices.

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a reclaim batch spans multiple non-full clusters, which can lead to scattered writes and readahead requests.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti expressed interest in the proposed solution and asked for more information about alternative fragmentation solutions.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Kairui,

On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 5:27 PM Kairui Song <ryncsn@gmail.com> wrote:

---

Oh, okay. I thought reverting it wasn't an option given the good
numbers the patch provides.

What are the other fragmentation solutions you are referring to?

Thanks,

Alex

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed concerns that the proposed solution of allocating contiguous swap slots may not address the underlying issue and could lead to increased memory overhead, scanning overhead, etc., suggesting that physical swap space compaction is still a problem and virtual swap space would just shift the issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hmm what other way are you thinking of? Physical swap space compaction
requires vswap, which has not landed. And we'd just be kicking the
problem to virtual swap space. Sure, we won't be failing allocation,
but that would still increase the memory overhead, scanning overhead,
etc.

I encountered this myself. Remember when I wrote my own swap allocator
for vswap? In one of the version, I went for free clusters first
instead of partial clusters. It fragmented the swap space, so I had to
copy your homework and went for partially used clusters first...

Anyway, maybe I'm wrong - some numbers would be nice here.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 7/7] btrfs: remove block_group data_rwsem and delalloc_bytes

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 7/7] btrfs: remove block_group data_rwsem and delalloc_bytes

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch removes the `data_rwsem` and `delalloc_bytes` fields from the Btrfs block group data structure, as they are no longer needed after the removal of the v1 space cache in a previous commit. The `data_rwsem` was only used by the v1 space cache write path, which has been removed, and `delalloc_bytes` is now only printed but not used. Removing these fields simplifies the code and eliminates confusing indirection machinery dedicated to separating delalloc calls from non-delalloc calls.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 6/7] btrfs: find_free_extent checks size class unlocked

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 6/7] btrfs: find_free_extent checks size class unlocked

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the find_free_extent function in Btrfs to skip block groups that have an incorrect size class without acquiring a lock on the block group. This is done to improve performance by reducing the number of locks taken, especially in large file systems where thousands of block groups may need to be checked. The patch also includes benchmarking results showing improved performance after applying this change.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 5/7] btrfs: find_free_extent checks full block groups unlocked

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 5/7] btrfs: find_free_extent checks full block groups unlocked

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the btrfs find_free_extent function by skipping block groups that are full and cannot satisfy an allocation request, without taking a lock. This is done because checking if a block group can satisfy an allocation does not guarantee that it will be able to do so when locked later. The patch also includes performance measurements showing significant improvements in certain scenarios.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 4/7] btrfs: factor the find_free_extent() block group skip into a helper

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 4/7] btrfs: factor the find_free_extent() block group skip into a helper

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors a complex condition in the find_free_extent() function into a separate helper function called find_free_extent_skip_block_group(). This makes the code easier to understand and maintain by breaking down a large, unwieldy block of logic into smaller, more manageable pieces. The new function checks if a block group can be skipped due to read-only status or other conditions, and returns true if it should be skipped. No functional changes are made.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 3/7] btrfs: remove redundant checks in find_free_extent() hint path

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 3/7] btrfs: remove redundant checks in find_free_extent() hint path

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch removes redundant checks in the find_free_extent() function's hint path, making it more efficient and reducing unnecessary complexity. The hint is a long-lasting reference to a block group that can outlast its destruction or be destroyed while still referenced. The patch simplifies the check for hints by only verifying their attachment to the list of block groups, allowing shared checks with normally reached block groups. This change improves code organization and reduces potential bugs caused by redundant checks.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 2/7] btrfs: don't take block group references in find_free_extent()

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 2/7] btrfs: don't take block group references in find_free_extent()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the find_free_extent() function in Btrfs by removing unnecessary get/put pairs on block group references. The get/put pair was pointless because the loop is already protected by a semaphore, making it impossible for this to be the last reference. This change saves time on filesystems with many full block groups and reduces the overhead of managing block group references.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 1/7] btrfs: skip unhelpful size class relaxing allocation loops

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 1/7] btrfs: skip unhelpful size class relaxing allocation loops

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the Btrfs extent tree by skipping unnecessary loops when size class is not a factor. It introduces a new flag to track whether a block group was skipped due to its size class, and only runs loops that are relevant based on this information. This change aims to reduce unnecessary computations and improve performance in certain scenarios.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 0/7] btrfs: allocator perf improvements
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of Btrfs's allocator by reducing unnecessary operations on block groups, particularly in large and mostly full file systems. The changes include skipping unhelpful size class relaxing allocation loops, removing redundant checks, and optimizing the find_free_extent function to skip locked block groups and size classes. These improvements result in significant speedups for certain workloads, such as running 20k fallocates on a sparse file system, which was previously taking around 40 seconds but is now completed in about 7 seconds.
